target.title: fix(signal): add timeouts to container REST requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Signal container REST requests already had a timeout around the fetch/header phase, but the timer was cleared as soon as response headers arrived. A response body that then stopped producing bytes could still leave REST status/send and attachment paths pending indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Preserve the existing fetch/header deadline, then apply the shared progress-aware body reader idle timeout to Signal REST success bodies, REST error bodies, and attachment downloads. This avoids the earlier total-response-deadline shape: a slow response can still succeed as long as chunks continue arriving before the idle timeout.

## User Impact

If the signal-cli REST container returns headers and then stalls, OpenClaw now fails the stalled body read instead of leaving Signal operations pending. Slow-but-progressing responses continue to work.

## Evidence

- Current head: `320766c17e73f422dd9f726bac36e68e7a54483f`.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed: 1 file, 65 tests.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed.
- `node_modules/.bin/oxlint extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts extensions/signal/src/client-container.test.ts` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- GitHub CI for this head is green: `gh pr checks 104122 --repo openclaw/openclaw` completed with no failed/pending checks.

Current-head local real HTTP harness proof:

```text
node --import tsx <<'HARNESS'
# temporary stdin harness; starts a redacted localhost HTTP server and calls
# containerRestRequest/containerFetchAttachment from extensions/signal/src/client-container.ts
HARNESS
```

Transcript:

```text
local Signal REST harness: direct containerRestRequest/containerFetchAttachment against redacted localhost server
stalled-success-body timeoutMs=80: error in 125ms Error: Signal REST response body stalled after 80ms
slow-success-body chunks every 40ms timeoutMs=80: ok in 210ms {"ok":true}
stalled-error-body timeoutMs=80: error in 85ms Error: Signal REST 500: Internal Server Error
stalled-attachment-body timeoutMs=80: error in 85ms Error: Signal REST attachment response body stalled after 80ms
```

Observations:

- This is real local HTTP behavior through the Signal REST client helpers, not a mocked fetch adapter.
- It proves the patched idle timeout aborts stalled success/error/attachment response bodies.
- It proves a slow response whose chunks continue arriving every 40ms succeeds even though total transfer time exceeds the 80ms idle timeout.

Not tested: a credentialed signal-cli REST container account was not available in this workspace; the live proof uses a redacted local HTTP server to exercise the exact REST client boundary.
